uncited: This method loads a single PNG image containing stacked 2D volume slices, parses its dimensions to reconstruct the 3D volume, converts pixel data to floating-point scalars, applies optional filtering, and optionally saves the result as a binary volume file.

It differs from [DICOM Slice Processing](6713-dicom-slice-processing.md) by handling raw raster images rather than medical metadata, and from [Slice to Binary Volume Conversion](6714-slice-to-binary-volume-conversion.md) by accepting a single multi-slice image file rather than a directory of individual slice files.
This variant handles more complex layouts including RGBA images, multi-frame sources, and grid-based slice arrangements.

It determines slice origins based on layout (vertical strip, horizontal strip, or grid), extracts individual slices from the image, and supports multi-file imports where each file is a separate frame.
- Time Complexity: Linear with respect to the number of pixels in the input image for loading and conversion.
- Memory Complexity: Proportional to the volume size ($X \times Y \times Z$) for storing the `scalars` vector.
It is designed for basic volume visualization where data is pre-packaged into a single image file for ease of distribution.
